name: Thali Time
subject: Indian food
tagline: Eleven questions on dal, dosas, street food and the spices that run the kitchen. A theme the group voted for. Starts easy, ends hard.

questions.q: Naan, the soft leavened flatbread, is traditionally baked by slapping it onto the wall of what?
questions.w: A tandoor, a bell-shaped clay oven that can reach 480 degrees Celsius, where the dough puffs and blisters in under a minute.
questions.more: Roti and chapati are unleavened and cooked on a tawa, which is why every home has one and few have a tandoor. The word naan is Persian for bread; the teardrop shape comes from the dough stretching as it is lowered onto the oven wall. Tandoor-cooked chicken, marinated in yoghurt and spices, is what gave the world tandoori chicken in the 1940s.

questions.w: A fresh, unsalted cheese made by curdling milk with lemon juice or vinegar and pressing the curds. It does not melt, so it can be fried and grilled.
questions.more: Because it needs no rennet, paneer suits India's many vegetarians, and it is the main protein in north Indian dishes such as palak paneer and paneer tikka. It is almost unknown in the south, where protein comes from lentils and coconut. The name shares a root with the Persian word for cheese.

questions.q: The sweet, spiced, milky tea sold at every Indian railway station is called what?
questions.w: Masala chai, black tea boiled with milk, sugar and spices such as cardamom, ginger and cloves.
questions.more: 'Chai' simply means tea, so 'chai tea' means tea tea. Indians drank little tea until the British-owned Indian Tea Association pushed it in the early 1900s; vendors then added milk and spices to stretch the expensive leaves, which the association disapproved of. Station chai was long served in small unglazed clay cups, thrown away and trodden back into the earth.

questions.q: A dosa, the crisp South Indian crêpe, is made from a fermented batter of rice and what?
questions.w: Urad dal, a skinned black lentil, soaked and ground with rice and left overnight to ferment, which gives the sour tang.
questions.more: The same batter, steamed instead of spread, becomes idli. A masala dosa is folded around spiced potatoes and served with sambar and coconut chutney; it is breakfast across Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. Dosas appear in Tamil literature from the first centuries AD, making them one of the world's oldest documented dishes.

questions.q: Ghee, used for everything from frying to temple lamps, is what?
questions.w: Clarified butter: butter simmered until the water boils off and the milk solids brown and sink, leaving a nutty golden fat that keeps for months without a fridge.
questions.more: Removing the milk solids raises the smoke point to about 250 degrees, higher than most oils, and removes nearly all the lactose. Ghee is sacred in Hinduism; it feeds the fire in wedding rituals and is one of the five products of the cow in panchamrit. India produces and eats more of it than the rest of the world combined.

questions.q: Biryani is widely believed to have been brought to India by which rulers, whose Persian-influenced court cuisine it reflects?
questions.w: The Mughals, in the 1500s and 1600s. The name comes from the Persian 'birinj', rice, or 'biryan', to fry before cooking.
questions.more: Legend credits Mumtaz Mahal, for whom the Taj Mahal was built, with ordering a one-pot dish to feed undernourished soldiers. Every region now claims its own: Hyderabad layers raw marinated meat under rice, Lucknow cooks them separately and seals the pot with dough, and Kolkata adds a potato, a thrift measure from the exiled court of Awadh. It is the most ordered dish on Indian delivery apps.

questions.q: In Kerala, the celebratory vegetarian feast of more than twenty dishes served on a banana leaf is called what?
questions.w: Sadya, eaten with the right hand and served in a fixed order, from pickles at the top of the leaf to payasam, the sweet pudding, at the end.
questions.more: It is the centrepiece of Onam, the Kerala harvest festival, when the state gets through hundreds of millions of banana leaves in a week. Folding the leaf towards you afterwards signals you enjoyed it; away from you, that you did not. A thali is the everyday equivalent on a steel plate; a langar is the free kitchen of a Sikh gurdwara.

questions.q: Which hollow, crisp puri is filled with spiced potato and a shot of tangy, minty water and eaten in one bite from street carts across India?
o: Pani puri, also called golgappa or puchka
questions.w: Pani puri, called golgappa in Delhi, puchka in Kolkata and gupchup in Odisha. The vendor cracks the shell with a thumb, stuffs it and dunks it in a pot of flavoured water.
questions.more: The waters range from tamarind-sweet to fiercely spiced with green chilli and black salt, and regulars specify the mix. Hygiene jokes about the vendor's thumb are part of the ritual; in 2024 the dish got its own Google doodle. Vada pav, a fried potato dumpling in a bun, is Mumbai's answer, and bhel puri is a puffed-rice salad from the same beaches.

questions.q: Which spice, worth more than its weight in gold in medieval Europe, grows only on the Malabar coast and was the main reason Vasco da Gama sailed to India in 1498?
questions.w: Black pepper, the 'black gold' of Kerala. Da Gama is said to have announced on landing at Calicut that he had come 'in search of Christians and spices'.
questions.more: Peppercorns were used as currency and rent in Rome and the Middle Ages, which is where 'peppercorn rent' comes from. The Portuguese, Dutch and then the British fought for the trade, and the British East India Company's first voyages were spice runs. Vietnam now out-produces India, but Tellicherry pepper from Kerala is still the prized grade.

questions.q: Idli, sambar and the fermented batter of the south rely on a culture of wild yeasts and bacteria. Which spice, with a famously eggy sulphur smell, is added to many lentil dishes to aid digestion?
questions.w: Asafoetida, or hing, a dried resin from a giant fennel-like plant. Raw it smells of rotten eggs; fried in hot oil it turns into something like onion and garlic.
questions.more: That is why it is prized by Jains and some Hindu Brahmins, whose diets forbid onion and garlic. Almost all of India's supply is imported from Afghanistan and Iran; the first Indian crop was planted in the Himalayas only in 2020. The Romans used it as a substitute for the extinct spice silphium.

questions.q: Which of these dishes come from Goa, with its Portuguese influence? Select all that apply.
questions.w: Sorpotel, bebinca and xacuti are Goan. Rogan josh is a Kashmiri lamb dish and dhokla is a steamed Gujarati chickpea cake.
questions.more: The Portuguese ruled Goa for 450 years, until 1961, and left pork, vinegar, bread and the chilli itself, which they brought from the Americas; the Goan pão bread is still baked by poders who blow a horn in the lane each morning. Bebinca is baked one layer at a time, traditionally sixteen of them, in a wood-fired oven. Sorpotel is made ahead and improves for days.
